Extract the tables of a co-occurrence network

Source: R/methods.R
as.data.frame.cooccurrence.Rd

as.data.frame() returns a table of a co-occurrence network as a plain data frame without the network's attributes, ready for sorting, joining, plotting or writing to a file. A co-occurrence network is described by two tables: its edges, one row per pair of items with a weight and a raw count, and its nodes, one row per item with degree, strength and frequency. A network built with split_by adds a third, one row of metrics per group.

what selects the table. The edge table is the printed network; the node and group tables are those of summary.cooccurrence().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cooccurrence'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what = c("edges", "nodes", "groups"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A cooccurrence edge list from cooccurrence().

row.names, optional

Unused; present for compatibility with the base::as.data.frame() generic.

what

"edges" (default), "nodes" or "groups".

...

Ignored.

Value

A base data.frame. For what = "edges", one row per edge with columns from, to, weight and count (and group for a split_by result), in the order printed. An undirected network has one row per pair; the directed similarity = "relative" network has one row per direction. For what = "nodes" and what = "groups", the tables described in as.data.frame.summary.cooccurrence().

See also

summary.cooccurrence(); as_matrix() for the weight matrix.

Examples

net <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                    similarity = "jaccard", min_occur = 50)
as.data.frame(net)
